tree.  CA- dry rocky slopes, forests, pj woodland.  At 1000-3000 m elevation on dry rocky slopes (Adams 1993).  In the Sierra Nevada, it grows on shallow soils, often with Abies magnifica, Pinus albicaulis, Pinus contorta subsp. murrayana, Pinus jeffreyi, or Tsuga mertensiana (Sowder and Mowat 1965).  At the southern extension of its range in San Bernardino County, it generally grows at a higher elevation than Juniperus californica and J. osteosperma (Munz and Keck 1959). This is the only documented area where J. occidentalis and Pinus monophylla grow together in a piñon-juniper woodland, although their distributions overlap geographically near the west edge of Nevada and from east-central to southern California (Griffin and Critchfield 1972, Horton 1960).
